name: Should I choose the lowest construction estimate?

mainEntity.name: Is the lowest estimate usually the best value for a home remodel or custom build?
mainEntity.text: Is the lowest estimate usually the best value for a home remodel or custom build?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lowest estimate is only the best value if it matches the same scope, quality, and assumptions as the other proposals. In many construction projects, the cheapest bid is low because it leaves out items, uses unrealistic allowances, or assumes the owner will pay extra later. This is especially risky in luxury or custom projects where finish quality matters and change orders can get expensive. A strong estimate should be transparent about what is included, what is excluded, and how uncertain items are priced. Owners in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood should compare completeness before comparing totals. If a bid is much lower than the others, ask where the savings come from and whether the estimate includes proper contingency, permit fees, and site work. The best value is usually the most complete and predictable number, not the smallest headline price.
acceptedAnswer.description: Not always. The lowest estimate may exclude key items, use low allowances, or assume a different scope than the other bids. The best value is the proposal that matches the drawings, includes realistic allowances, and explains exclusions clearly.
